answer: Each identity seats a quartz crystal in an inlet, locks 70 credits, and files a key-bound serial. The kernel presses it each epoch, logging the piezo charge. An auditor recomputes the charge from the public quartz piezo table; over 3% off, a reused serial, or one crystal filed twice burns the bond. Filing costs 45 first, 45+4(k-1) for the k-th; the 1000th pays 4,041, 1000 fakes pay 2,043,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-reading ring fails: one crystal yields one kernel-signed reading per serial, yet each fake pays its own fee. An honest identity pays 45 once, bond back after a clean epoch.
